insights.headline: Gold holds above $4,150 and silver snaps its losing streak as falling yields blunt the Fed-hike scare
insights.summary: Gold extended Thursday's rebound into the US session, holding above $4,150 as an AI-led equity selloff pulled the 10-year Treasury yield to a three-week low and the dollar off an 18-month peak. COMEX silver snapped a three-day losing streak with a 2.3% gain to settle at $56.84. Hot September inflation data — CPI at 3.7% and PPI up 6.3% on the year — kept October Fed-hike bets near 30%, capping the rally. In India, MCX gold traded near ₹1.47 lakh per 10 grams and silver near ₹2.09 lakh per kg, while mutual funds halted bulk gold-ETF subscriptions ahead of the festive season.
points: Gold's rebound ran through the US session as the AI equity selloff deepened and haven demand offset hot-inflation pressure.
Silver settled 2.3% higher at $56.84, its biggest one-day gain since October 9, after a 6% plunge on the CPI shock.
September CPI of 3.7% and PPI up 6.3% kept October Fed-hike odds near 30%, with officials split on further tightening.
MCX gold held near ₹1.47 lakh and silver near ₹2.09 lakh; mutual funds paused bulk gold-ETF subscriptions before the festive rush.
India's gold imports fell 27% after the customs duty hike to 15%, while festive jewellery demand showed early recovery.

trending.title: Haven bid back as the AI selloff spreads
trending.summary: Gold held above $4,150 and silver posted its best day in a week as sliding Treasury yields and a weaker dollar pulled investors toward havens while tech stocks sank.

trending.title: Hot inflation keeps the Fed-hike debate alive
trending.summary: September CPI at 3.7% and PPI up 6.3% on the year kept October hike odds near 30%, leaving bullion's rebound fragile as traders await the next Fed signals.

trending.title: India's festive demand meets supply caution
trending.summary: Mutual funds halted bulk gold-ETF subscriptions and imports fell 27% after the duty hike, even as jewellery demand showed early signs of recovery.

trending.title: Silver's whiplash week
trending.summary: A 6% CPI-driven plunge gave way to a 2.3% bounce, while a 41% output drop at Mexico's San Dimas mine underscored supply tightness.

items.title: Gold Rallies, Silver Doesn't as Tech Stocks Sink with Bond Yields
items.summary: Gold rallied to $4,150 at London's Thursday 3pm fix as long-term bond yields fell at their fastest pace in two years, rebounding from a 10-week low of $4,089 on Wednesday. Silver diverged sharply, touching a three-month low of $55.41 as a credit scare around AI data-centre company CoreWeave rattled tech stocks. The gold/silver ratio rose above 73, its highest since December 2025.

items.title: Indian mutual funds stop bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festive season
items.summary: Several large fund houses, including Kotak Mahindra, UTI and HDFC Mutual Fund, issued notices late on Thursday halting bulk subscriptions to their gold ETFs as festive-season demand picks up; redemptions are unaffected. The move followed a nudge from SEBI, and bullion dealers read it as a precautionary step to avoid an October import surge after September's Rs 4,451 crore of net ETF inflows.

items.title: Gold holding overnight gains above $4,100 even as US PPI rises 6.3% in September
items.summary: US producer prices jumped 1.3% in September, the largest monthly rise since March 2022, lifting annual wholesale inflation to 6.3% against a 5.3% consensus. Gold nevertheless held overnight gains above $4,100, trading near $4,152, as a pullback in Treasury yields and a softer dollar blunted the impact of the hot print. Silver also rebounded after its 6% post-CPI plunge.

items.title: Comex Silver Settles 2.32% Higher at $56.837 — Data Talk
items.summary: Front-month COMEX silver for October delivery settled $1.29 (2.3%) higher at $56.84 on Thursday, snapping a three-session losing streak with its biggest one-day gain since October 9. The bounce tracked a softer dollar off an 18-month peak and a slide in Treasury yields to a three-week low, though silver remains down about 19% so far in 2026 and roughly half its January record.

items.title: India’s gold imports drop 27% after customs duty hike to 15%
items.summary: Commerce Ministry data shows India’s gold imports fell to $19.27 billion in April–September 2026 from $26.51 billion a year earlier, after customs duty on gold and silver was raised to 15% in May. September saw declines in both gold and silver imports, while the merchandise trade deficit narrowed to $30.21 billion.

items.title: Gold falls below $4,100, silver plunges 6% as hot CPI boosts Fed-hike bets - Kitco PM Report
items.summary: Gold and silver fell sharply in late US trading on Wednesday after hotter-than-expected US inflation lifted Treasury yields and the dollar. Spot gold traded near $4,098.80, down $61.30 (1.47%); spot silver near $55.41, down $3.64 (6.16%), with selling accelerating across precious metals. The S&P 500 fell 1.1% in its worst day since July.

items.title: Silver Faces Fresh Inflation Test After September PPI Jumps 1.3%
items.summary: September US producer prices jumped 1.3% m/m and 6.3% y/y - the largest monthly rise since March 2022 - with energy up 10.8%, putting silver under a fresh inflation test as it tries to stabilize near $55. FXEmpire notes persistent inflation could keep financing costs elevated, a headwind for non-yielding silver and for industrial users' inventory decisions.

items.title: Gold price forecast: Why investors expect record highs within 2 years
items.summary: Fund managers at the FT's precious metals symposium expect gold to hit record highs within 12 to 24 months, citing rising US debt, de-dollarisation and geopolitical risk. Troy's Charlotte Yonge pointed to the US fiscal outlook; Aon's Paul Carne said weaponising the dollar pushes investors toward gold. Central banks bought about 63 tonnes in September, the strongest month since November 2024 (WGC).

items.title: MCX Gold trade above ₹1.47 lakh per 10 gram, Silver rebounds from ₹2.11 lakh support; check trade setup for Oct 15
items.summary: MCX gold December futures rose 1.4% to ₹1,47,916 per 10 grams as value buying returned after the hot-CPI selloff, aided by a softer dollar; silver December futures gained 1.3% to ₹2,11,119 per kg after rebounding off the ₹2.11 lakh support. The session piece maps key intraday support and resistance levels for Oct 15.

items.title: Gold eyes sharp recovery; can MCX prices hit Rs 1.5 lakh? Vandana Bharti explains
items.summary: MCX gold futures rose 1.17% to Rs 1,47,558 per 10 grams on October 15 as global prices recovered. Vandana Bharti of SMC Global Securities expects MCX gold to hold in the Rs 1,45,000-1,50,000 range, with Rs 1.5 lakh the top of that band rather than a clean breakout; she cautions that a stronger rupee could limit how much of the global rebound reaches domestic prices.

items.title: Gold prices fall 1 percent on MCX as rupee's sharp appreciation weighs on bullion
items.summary: Gold traded weak on October 14 as the rupee's sharp appreciation against the dollar pressured domestic bullion ahead of the US CPI release. MCX spot gold slipped 1.03% to Rs 1,45,615 per 10 grams while December futures eased 0.33% to Rs 1,47,956; international spot gold held just above $4,150 an ounce. items.title: Sky Gold surges 26% in October; stock up over 3-fold thus far in FY27
items.summary: Shares of gold-jewellery manufacturer Sky Gold hit a new high of Rs 1,021.95 on Thursday, up 26% in October and 3.2-fold since March, as organised jewellery retail keeps gaining share. The B2B maker supplies chains such as Joyalukkas, Malabar and Senco Gold and is expanding exports via its Dubai office, targeting about a fifth of sales overseas by FY30.

items.title: Silver Output at Mexico's San Dimas Mine Fell 41%, and Now It Has Stopped
items.summary: First Majestic's San Dimas silver mine in Mexico is on formal strike since October 8, with about 800 union workers citing safety and contract breaches; extraction stays halted. The mine produced 41% less silver in Q3 than a year earlier, per the company's release, which blames 12 lost days and lower grades. More strikes would widen silver's forecast 46.3-million-ounce 2026 deficit.

items.title: DGFT Speeds Up Silver Imports Through IIBX & Nominated Agencies
items.summary: DGFT’s Trade Notice No. 30/2026-27 (13 October 2026) introduced a simplified, expedited procedure for silver import authorisations covering specified ITC(HS) codes, excluding silver dore. Applicants must declare imports at the generally applicable duty rate and justify quantities; each authorisation is valid for six months. Silver must be procured only through IIBX or nominated banks and agencies.

items.title: RBI sets ₹14,725 premature redemption price for SGB 2019-20 Series V
items.summary: RBI fixed the premature redemption price of Sovereign Gold Bond 2019-20 Series V at ₹14,725 per unit for redemption due on October 15, 2026, the simple average of IBJA's 999-purity gold closes over the three business days before redemption. ET reported the exit turns a ₹1 lakh 2019 investment into about ₹3.94 lakh, a ~294% return before the 2.5% annual interest.

items.title: Pralhad Joshi Launches Silver Refinery Certification Scheme
items.summary: Consumer Affairs Minister Pralhad Joshi launched a BIS certification scheme for silver refineries and mints at a World Standards Day event in New Delhi. Under the scheme, BIS will license qualified facilities, bringing silver bullion and coins under hallmarking-style purity and traceability checks; he also announced seven new Indian Standards and a Digital Standard Reader.

items.title: China Is Aggressively Buying Gold As Prices Fall. Should Indian Buyers Be Worried Or Hopeful?
items.summary: China is aggressively adding gold to its reserves even as prices fall — a long-term strategic move rather than a short-term trade, News18 reports. The buying could put a floor under prices but guarantees nothing, so Indian buyers may see some relief without a price collapse.

items.title: Iran shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping before US vote, officials say
items.summary: Iran is deploying new tactics to target ships in the Strait of Hormuz to keep oil prices high and influence the US midterm elections, two senior Iranian officials told Reuters. Tehran has restricted the strait since US-Israeli strikes on February 28, with attacks stepping up about 10 days ago. Energy-led inflation risk complicates the Fed's path and keeps a defensive bid under gold.

items.title: US labour market stuck in low-hire, low-fire state as inflation intensifies: Fed Beige Book
items.summary: The Federal Reserve’s Beige Book showed a stagnant US labour market with intensifying price pressures from energy, tariffs and insurance costs, complicating the case for policymakers weighing an October rate hike. It follows September CPI of 3.7% and last month’s 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%; the 30-year US mortgage rate hit 7.5%, its highest in nearly three years.

items.title: Gold jewellery gets costlier as prices surge 54%; shoppers turn to Rs 10,000-Rs 1 lakh diamond pieces
items.summary: With gold prices up 54%, Indian shoppers are shifting to diamond pieces priced ₹10,000–₹1 lakh, which jewellers are making accessible in 18, 14 and even 9-carat gold, the Times of India reports. Joyalukkas has seen an uptick in diamond sales and Senco expects 20% growth in diamond jewellery this festive season.

items.title: Gold Jewellery Demand Recovers as Prices Ease
items.summary: Gold jewellery demand is recovering as prices ease from record highs, with buyers resuming purchases they had postponed. Sales at Delhi's Dariba Kalan market rose nearly 20%. In the June quarter, Kalyan Jewellers' India revenue grew over 38% with same-store sales up 28%, while Titan and Senco Gold also reported strong growth.

items.title: India's hidden gold chest is giving imported bullion a run for its money
items.summary: Soaring prices are pushing Indians to exchange old jewellery for new designs rather than cut festive purchases, the Economic Times reports. Old-gold exchanges accounted for over 50% of transactions at Tanishq, more than 55% of sales at Kalyan Jewellers and 73% at Joyalukkas in August — recycled domestic supply that softens import demand.

items.title: Decoding India's inflation: Onions, silver key drivers; more storage capacity will make RBI's task easier
items.summary: September CPI inflation of 5.54% was driven by rising onion and silver prices along with related transport costs, ThePrint reports. Building more onion storage capacity would make the RBI's inflation-management task easier — a reminder that silver's rally feeds directly into India's price pressures.
